source_identity.name: Geo-referencing of Ethnic Groups (GREG)
source_identity.source_atlas: Bruk, Solomon I. and V. S. Apenchenko (eds.), Atlas narodov mira / Atlas of the Peoples of the World, Moscow, 1964
source_identity.research_article: Weidmann, Nils B., Jan Ketil Rød, Lars-Erik Cederman. “Representing Ethnic Groups in Space: A New Dataset.” Journal of Peace Research 47(4), 491–499. Published online 2010-05-25; issue date 2010-07-01. DOI 10.1177/0022343310368352.
source_identity.current_version_notice: GREG page says an up-to-date version of the dataset is at the EPR GeoEPR page; this bounded review evaluates the explicitly selected GREG ZIP, not the later/current GeoEPR product.
source_identity.scope: Global GREG release (8,969 polygons); bounded example subset is 25 source polygon records intersecting the rectangular query envelope [−5,4,5,15] degrees WGS84. This envelope is a retrieval window only, not an Atlas boundary or region definition.

edition_dates.underlying_observation_date: No polygon-specific date. Article says the source ANM maps were collected in the early 1960s; exact underlying observations vary and are not specified per polygon.
edition_dates.GREG_shapefile_archive_metadata: DBF_DATE_LAST_UPDATE 2008-11-01; ZIP member timestamps from 2008. These are file/edition metadata, not group observation dates.
edition_dates.site_imprint: © 2023 ETH Zurich on accessed page; not a dataset release or dataset rights notice.

license_assessment.status: unverified; no dataset-specific reuse license found in the inspected public data page, shapefile archive/XML, online appendix, or paper.
license_assessment.public_access: GREG ZIP and group list are directly downloadable without authentication.
license_assessment.citation_request: The GREG page requests citation to Weidmann, Rød and Cederman (2010), JPR 47(4):491–499.
license_assessment.rights_distinction: Public download and a citation request do not state rights to redistribute or adapt the dataset. The journal article’s standard publication-reuse rights metadata and the ETH website imprint are not a dataset license. The 1964 atlas is a distinct upstream work; no permission to reproduce it was found.
license_assessment.decision: Do not bundle source files or geometry, redistribute the global dataset, or treat the license as open. Keep only this bounded research evidence and exact restoration/hash notes. Seek rights-holder clarification before reuse or import.

schema.coordinate_reference_system: WGS84 / EPSG:4326 (verified from GREG.prj and GDAL)

fields.G1ID,G2ID,G3ID: group IDs; zero means not applicable; each polygon has one to three group identifiers; G1ID is never zero
fields.AREA: source polygon area in square metres, computed in Eckert VI equal-area projection
fields.COW: 1989 Correlates of War country code context

schema.population_shares: No population or group-share field in the inspected shapefile schema. The research article says source maps can show up to three groups sharing a territory; it provides no polygon-level relative share. G1/G2/G3 are identifiers, not population ranks or proportions.
schema.primary_culture: Not defined by GREG; ethnic group labels cannot be promoted to a single primary culture using order, polygon area, or overlap.

method_and_uncertainty.production: Authors scanned 57 ANM ethnographic maps, georeferenced them in GIS using WGS84 latitude/longitude, distributed ground-control points (usually about 20/map), applied affine transformation, visually checked fit, and digitized areas. English group names were assigned using ANM translations.
method_and_uncertainty.positional_rule_of_thumb: Appendix estimates 0.5 mm map position error; at 1:15,000,000 this is 7.5 km, and gives about 10 km as a conservative general assessment. This is not a measured per-feature uncertainty or confidence interval.
method_and_uncertainty.temporal_caveat: The source represents a static map compiled in the early 1960s; no dated snapshots or per-feature observation intervals. The article warns that conflict and forced movement can make configurations outdated.
method_and_uncertainty.selection: GDAL spatial-filter query window [−5,4,5,15] degrees WGS84; export intersecting features in source order and retain the first 25. The sample is purposive and non-random; no geometry or whole dataset is retained. This is not zonal allocation or an Atlas territorial definition.
